evidence: Sen. Ep. 84.8: imāgō rēs mortua est
terms.comment: Latin often leaves the noun out and lets a neuter pronoun or adjective stand for “thing”: quid est hoc?, what’s this?; multa, many things. Rēs is also the matter in hand and the state of affairs (see situation).

phrases.latin: jacēs indignō quanta rēs, inquit, locō!
phrases.english: “What a fine thing you are,” he said, “to be lying in so poor a place!”

phrases.latin: similem esse tē volō quōmodo fīlium, nōn quōmodo imāginem: imāgō rēs mortua est
phrases.english: I want you to be like me as a son is, not as a portrait is: a portrait is a dead thing

phrases.latin: quaesō, inquit, quid est hoc, Pȳthī? tantumne piscium? tantumne cumbārum?
phrases.english: “Please, what is all this, Pythius?” he said. “So many fish? So many boats?”
